title: Haul Away Joe
origin: Traditional short-drag halyard shanty of the merchant service

pd.detail: Traditional short-drag halyard shanty documented in the British and American merchant service from the mid nineteenth century, in oral circulation well before 1900. No identifiable author.
pd.sourceEdition: Traditional; encoded from the common version preserved in the pre-1930 shanty collections (Whall, 'Ships, Sea Songs and Shanties', 1910; Terry, 'The Shanty Book', 1921-1926)
pd.notes: The words carry their own separate public-domain basis in each section's lyrics.pd; this block covers the music only. Encoded as the traditional version, not any twentieth-century arrangement or recording. The tune is duple and is notated in common time in the standard collections; the characteristic lilt is carried by feel = swing on plain eighths rather than by dotted figures, so nothing sits off the 16th grid. The pull of the crew falls on the first accented note of the refrain and again on its final long note.

pd.detail: Anonymous short-drag shanty text of the British and American merchant service, with no identifiable author; documented from the mid nineteenth century and in oral circulation well before 1900.
pd.sourceEdition: Terry, 'The Shanty Book' Part II, 1926, No. 35 ('Haul away, Joe. II'), verses 4-5; Part I, 1921, No. 28, verses 3-4; the same verses in Whall, 'Ships, Sea Songs and Shanties', 1910, p. 117

lyrics.notes: Every line here is verbatim from Terry; nothing is reconstructed. Stanza 1 is Terry Part II verses 4-5, the King Louis pair, which Whall p. 117 prints as the same consecutive pair with the same answering chorus. Stanza 2 is Terry Part I verses 3-4, which Terry's own note at Part II No. 35 licenses being sung to this tune. The verse everyone opens with -- 'when I was a little boy ... my lips would all grow mouldy' -- is NOT in Whall, Terry Part I or Terry Part II; it surfaces only in mid-twentieth-century revival performances, so it cannot be vouched for from the cited printings and has been dropped. Terry Part I verses 5-6 and Terry Part II verses 2-3, and the matching pair in Whall, use a racial slur about a sweetheart; those are omitted entirely and are not rewritten into anything else. The crew answer falls on bars 2 and 6, where the pull lands on the accented first note.

stanzas.text: King Louis was the king o' France before the revolution
Away, haul away, Oh haul away, Joe
King Louis got his head cut off and spoiled his constitution
Away, haul away, Oh haul away, Joe
Way, haul away, we'll hang and haul together
Away, haul away, Oh haul away, Joe
Way, haul away, we'll haul for better weather
Away, haul away, Oh haul away, Joe

pd.detail: Anonymous short-drag shanty text of the British and American merchant service, with no identifiable author; the crew refrain is the fixed answer of the song as printed in the pre-1930 collections.
pd.sourceEdition: Terry, 'The Shanty Book' Part II, 1926, No. 35 ('Haul away, Joe. II'), verse 1; the same couplet in Whall, 'Ships, Sea Songs and Shanties', 1910, p. 117

lyrics.notes: One stanza: the refrain couplet is invariant, so both occurrences sing the same words. Transcribed verbatim as Terry Part II verse 1; Whall p. 117 prints the same couplet as 'Away, haul away, O haul away together / Away, haul away, O haul away, Jo!'. The crew pull falls on the accented first note of each line and again on its closing long note.

stanzas.text: Way, haul away, we'll haul away the bowlin'
Away, haul away, Oh haul away, Joe
